references.text: The preceding context establishing the punishment for giving children to Molech, which verse 4 refers to when the people turn a blind eye to this sin
The original prohibition against giving offspring to Molech, which forms the basis of the punishment described in chapter 20
The prohibition against letting children pass through the fire, a practice associated with Molech worship
King Josiah destroyed Topheth in the Valley of Hinnom to prevent child sacrifice to Molech
God's condemnation of those who built altars for Baal and sacrificed their children to Molech in the Valley of Hinnom
Ezekiel accuses the priests of turning a blind eye to God's Sabbaths, a parallel to ignoring sin
The warning that whoever turns a blind eye to the poor will be cursed, a principle about not ignoring injustice
Stephen mentions Molech worship in his speech concerning Israel's apostasy and idolatry
